subject: Information Theory
title: Deepfakes
description: A micro-lesson that makes Deepfakes usable.

hook.text: A deepfake video showed a world leader declaring war. It was fake—but millions believed it for hours.

buildup.text: Deepfakes use neural networks to generate realistic fake video and audio. The technology improves monthly.

discovery.text: The information-theoretic problem: as generation improves, the mutual information between fake and real approaches zero.

twist.text: Detection tools exist, looking for blink patterns and artifacts, but they're losing the arms race with generators.

climax.text: When any video could be fake, real evidence loses credibility too. This is the 'liar's dividend': doubt everything.

punchline.text: When fakes look real, real looks fake. Trust collapses.

quiz.question: What is the 'liar's dividend' of deepfake technology?
options: Real evidence loses credibility because anything could be faked
